llm_judge_reasons: Getter (get_history) correctly reads Chrome's SQLite History DB and returns (url, title, last_visit_time) tuples, giving the metric direct access to all stored URLs.
Metric (check_history_deleted) correctly extracts history[0] (url) from each tuple and checks if either keyword ('youtube' or 'cnn.com') appears in any remaining URL.

Parameter handling is correct: expected.type='rule' causes the framework to pass rules dict directly as the 'rule' parameter, so rule['type'] and rule['keywords'] are accessed correctly without the wrong expected.get('rules') anti-pattern.
Both instruction requirements are covered: 'youtube' keyword catches all youtube.com URLs, 'cnn.com' catches CNN URLs. Both must be absent for the check to pass (score=1.0).
Postconfig correctly kills and restarts Chrome before evaluation to release the SQLite lock, ensuring the getter can read the History file.
Non-target history entries (BBC, NYTimes, NatGeo) remain in the DB and do not cause false negatives, correctly allowing them to persist.

metadata.capability_extraction: Can filter Chrome history by site name, select all, and delete. Can repeat the process for a second domain.
metadata.explanation: Compound deletion task chaining the original YouTube-clearing objective with an additional CNN-clearing objective. Evaluator uses check_history_deleted with two keywords so both domains must be absent from history to pass. The agent must perform the search-select-delete workflow twice (once for youtube, once for cnn.com).
